newsitem.title: USA: Bob Evans Farms profits tumble in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Bob Evans Farms profits tumble in quarter.

text.p: Bob Evans Farms Inc., a restaurant operator and maker of sausages and charcoal, said Tuesday its quarterly profits tumbled as hog costs soared and sales at its older restaurants declined.

Net income fell 38 percent to $8.9 million, or 21 cents a share, in the quarter ended July 26 from $14.4 million, or 34 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales rose 4 percent to $213.1 million from $205.9 million.

The results were hurt by an 82 percent drop in profits at Bob Evans' food products division, which makes Hickory Specialities charcoal products. Hog costs, which account for most of the material cost of sausages, surged 47 percent over the 1995 quarter.
That offset a 9 percent rise in division revenues due to higher sausage wholesale prices and increased sales of charcoal products.

Profits at Bob Evans Restaurants fell 27 percent as same-store sales for outlets older than two years slid 3.2 percent, reducing margins. However, restaurant sales rose as the company expanded its network to 390 outlets in 18 states at the end of the quarter from 361 a year ago.
The Columbus, Ohio-based company said it plans to open 25 to 30 Bob Evans Restaurants during this fiscal year.
The company produces and distributes food products under the brand names of Bob Evans Farms Sausage, Owens Country Sausage, Mrs. Giles and Mrs. Kinser's in 29 states.
Bob Evans' stock fell 12.5 cents to $14.50 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
